title: Topology-aware load replayer for Private/VPC/on‑prem benchmarks
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Build a reproducible, topology-aware benchmarking harness that can be run against Private/VPC/on-prem environments to replay customer-like traffic and measure tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latencies, KV cache behavior, and system resource usage. The harness must minimize customer footprint, be deterministic across repeated runs, and integrate with CI to detect regressions against stored baselines.
technical_design: Harness will use a containerized workload runner plus environment fingerprinter. Components: (1) scenario compiler that converts customer traces or synthetic prompts into deterministic request sequences with seedable RNG and fixed timestamps; (2) topology emulator to reproduce network latency, bandwidth, and storage IOPS using tc/netem and fio scenarios; (3) workload orchestrator (ansible + terraform + k8s job) that deploys test harness in customer VPC or on-prem using a read-only agent; (4) metrics collector (prometheus + custom exporter) for tokens/sec, per-request latencies, p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, queue-length, and KV cache hit/miss; (5) result snapshotter that stores run artifacts in S3/MinIO and submits a diff to regression service.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic replay: same request stream + seed produces <=1% variance in tokens/sec across 3 runs
Topological fidelity: ability to inject measured network latency and bandwidth limits matching a provided network fingerprint
Metric coverage: tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, per-request token counts, GPU utilization, KV cache hit-rate reported
Automated regression: CI pipeline compares new run to baseline and flags >5% token/sec regression or >10% p95 increase
Minimal customer footprint: read-only agent deployable via single SSH command or CloudFormation/Terraform snippet
tasks: Design environment fingerprint schema (network, storage, CPU, driver versions)
Implement deterministic scenario compiler and seeding strategy
Prototype topology emulator using tc, netem, and tcconfig
Add prometheus exporters for tokens/sec and KV cache metrics
Create result snapshot format (JSON + compressed traces) and storage path
Integrate run into nightly CI with automatic baseline comparison
Document runbook and security model for private deployments
progress_updates: 2026-03-01: Kickoff meeting with Solutions and Security to define acceptable agent permissions and audit requirements
2026-03-03: Prototype scenario compiler that converts sample customer traces into seedable request files (PoC complete)
2026-03-05: Topology emulator spike validated netem-based latency injection on Linux kernels 5.x; edge-cases for Windows noted
2026-03-08: Prometheus exporter added for token throughput and p95 calculation; exporter tested in dev cluster
2026-03-10: Started CI integration; first deterministic run produced 0.8% variance in tokens/sec (within target)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Agent in customer VPC may require elevated network permissions — Mitigation: design as read-only, use ephemeral SSH tunneling and scoped IAM roles
Risk: Time sync variance affects deterministic replay — Mitigation: enforce NTP sync and include time offset normalization in compiler
Risk: Kernel versions/drivers produce variance — Mitigation: capture kernel/driver fingerprint and include in baseline metadata
Risk: Large customer traces produce heavy storage load — Mitigation: support sampling, trimming, and compressed trace formats
observability_and_alerting: Regression service will evaluate runs and write pass/fail to CI. Alerts: slack + pagerduty for high-severity regressions (tokens/sec drop >10% or p95 >20% increase). Results dashboard will show run-to-baseline delta for tokens/sec and p95 with histogram overlays.
runbook: Step 1: Acquire customer fingerprint (network, storage, CPU/GPU, OS, driver versions)
Step 2: Generate deterministic scenario with scenario-compiler --seed=<id>
Step 3: Deploy topology emulator and read-only agent using provided terraform/ansible scripts
Step 4: Start run with orchestrator; wait for warmup window (configurable default 120s)
Step 5: Collect metrics and snapshot, upload artifacts to results bucket
Step 6: CI compares to baseline and posts regression result to PR and dashboard
Step 7: If regression detected, run binary search smoke tests to narrow regression cause
notes_for_review: Need Security review for agent install flow and S3 artifact encryption
